items.stem: Which device forwards traffic BETWEEN different networks, choosing a path based on IP addresses?

options.rationale: Correct: a router forwards packets between networks using IP addressing.
A switch forwards frames within a single local network using MAC addresses.
A hub simply repeats signals to all ports within one segment.
A cable is a medium; it does not make forwarding decisions.

items.explanation: Correct: a router forwards packets between networks using IP addressing.

items.stem: Which statements correctly contrast TCP and UDP? (Select TWO)

options.text: TCP establishes a connection and retransmits lost data
options.rationale: Correct: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable.

options.text: UDP sends datagrams without guaranteeing delivery or order
options.rationale: Correct: UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery.
UDP does not provide encryption by itself.

options.text: TCP is faster than UDP because it does less work
options.rationale: TCP does more work (acknowledgements, ordering), so it is generally not faster than UDP.

items.explanation: Correct: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable.

items.stem: A PC gets an IP address but cannot resolve website names, though it can ping public IP addresses. What is the most likely cause?

options.rationale: Correct: reaching IPs but not names points to name resolution (DNS) failing.
A cable fault would usually stop all connectivity, including pinging IPs.
The PC has an IP and can reach IPs, so addressing is working.
If all traffic were blocked, pinging public IPs would also fail.

items.explanation: Correct: reaching IPs but not names points to name resolution (DNS) failing.
